text:
Liam: FYI customer atlas-inc reported a sudden p99 jump after we onboarded phoenix-1.2 to hosted. p95 stable (~320ms) but p99 went from ~450ms -> ~2.8s across several routes. Started ~2026-03-03 10:12 UTC.
Amy: Noted. Which routes? embeddings or /chat?
Liam: /chat streaming & non-streaming both. Long-context sessions (6k-10k tokens) seem worst. Short queries fine.
Morgan: Any consistent client pattern? large system prompts, lots of function calls?
Liam: Mostly long system+user history. One repro from atlas included a 9k-token context that spikes p99.
Raj: Jumping in — is this likely model runtime change or tokenizer? Phoenix-1.2 included a bpe-normalization tweak we pushed yesterday.
Eva: We rolled tokenizer normalizer patch to phoenix-1.2 to handle CJK edgecases. Could that increase token counts for certain sequences?
Liam: Yes, sample customer trace shows tokenized length increased ~18% for their historical context. That could change KV cache hit patterns.
Jules: If token count increases, KV cache boundaries shift — could cause cache misses and more compute per request; would inflate tail latency.
SRE-Bot: Autoscales triggered for phoenix-1.2 pool at 10:15 UTC (scale +2). Average GPU utilization ~86% after rollout.
Raj: I pulled a flamegraph for a repro request (trace id trace-0a7f). Long latency is dominated by attention kernel warmups and repeated KV cache re-allocs around token boundary.
Raj: attaching snippet of runtime logs (truncated):
```
[2026-03-03T10:14:52Z] trace=trace-0a7f stage=decode tokens_in=9187 tokens_out=102
[2026-03-03T10:14:52Z] runtime=attention kernel_init 0.67s
[2026-03-03T10:14:53Z] runtime=kvcache rebind 1.2s
[2026-03-03T10:14:54Z] runtime=generate 0.6s
```
Amy: So rebind hits are expensive when context length moves across preset buckets. Any quick mitigation?
Raj: Short-term: route atlas traffic to phoenix-1.1 (old tokenizer + same model weights) or downgrade tokenizer normalization on phoenix-1.2. Fastest is routing.
Liam: Customer asked for workaround ASAP. Can we do model routing flag?
Deploy-Bot: Routing change request queued by Amy — route atlas-inc -> phoenix-1.1 (traffic: 100%) on dedicated-hosted cluster alpha. ID: route-5231.
Amy: I'll notify atlas support contact and escalate SLA override.
Morgan: For medium-term fix we should: 1) add deterministic token-length map for common language families so kvcache bucket boundaries are stable; 2) adjust kvcache rebind path to be incremental (avoid full rebind cost); 3) test tokenizer normalization impact in onboarding harness.
Jules: Agree. Also add a temporary config to disable aggressive prefix caching for phoenix-1.2 until we confirm tokenization behavior. That reduces hot-path rebinds.
Raj: Repro steps I used (please run on staging):
1) curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.com/v1/chat 
   -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' 
   -d '{"model":"phoenix-1.2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<8k tokens system prompt>"}, {"role":"user","content":"<user history ~7k tokens>"}]}'
2) capture timings via X-Request-ID header and check runtime logs for kvcache rebind
3) compare token counts: run tokenizer on both phoenix-1.1 and phoenix-1.2 and diff lengths

I pushed a small repro script to staging gist: https://internal/gists/phoenix-token-repro (tokenize + timing).
Eva: I ran the tokenizer diff on a customer's export and saw 14-20% token inflation in worst-case sequences (mostly emoji + mixed CJK + diacritics).
Amy: Customer notified, we've routed them to phoenix-1.1, they confirmed drop in p99 to ~480ms after routing.
SRE-Bot: route-5231 deploy completed at 10:33 UTC. No errors.
Liam: Good. What's the rollback plan for phoenix-1.2? Do we revert normalization or patch runtime?
Raj: Plan: 1) Reproduce across at least 5 corpora, quantify token inflation buckets. 2) Implement a tokenizer change that preserves legacy BPE mapping for contexts >4k tokens (opt-in flag). 3) Improve kvcache rebind to stream incremental KV pages rather than full rebind. 4) Run synthetic long-context load test (4h) and measure p95/p99.
Jules: Timeline?
Raj: Small patch to tokenizer (opt-in legacy mapping) can go today to a canary: phoenix-1.2-legacy-tokenizer. Runtime kvcache incremental change is medium effort (1-2 sprints) but we can add mitigations like extending kvcache TTL boundaries to power-of-two buckets to reduce rebinds.
Morgan: For immediate release notes: mark phoenix-1.2 onboarding as WARNING for long-context customers until we confirm. Add a note to onboarding checklist: run token inflation check and p99 simulation.
Amy: I'll update the customer-facing ticket and post a KB: "If you see p99 increase after model update: request routing to last-stable model; share full chat export for tokenizer diff."
Liam: Any chance this also affects embeddings pipeline?
Raj: Embeddings use different tokenizer path; we saw no regression in embeddings p99. This looks specific to chat long-context path and KV cache interactions.
Eva: I'll prepare a unit test set with mixed CJK+emoji sequences to catch token inflation regressions in CI for future releases.
Amy: Summary for the ticket: customer routed to phoenix-1.1; investigational cause: tokenizer normalization increased token counts causing KV cache rebinds and runtime overhead at tail; mitigations: routing + canary legacy tokenizer + runtime kvcache fixes in backlog.
Liam: Thanks team. Please add any follow-ups to the ticket 98721 and assign owners.
Raj: Assigning myself for tokenizer patch PR and Morgan for kvcache design doc.
Deploy-Bot: PR created: github.com/redwood/phoenix-tokenizer/pull/411 (label: hotfix-canary).
Amy: I'll schedule a postmortem if we see any other customers affected. :thumbsup:
